speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your wife is concerned about your behavior; can you tell me what has been happening that led to her bringing you here?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that context. To help me understand your current state, are you currently experiencing any hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others do not? Additionally, have you had any changes in your sleep patterns or appetite recently?

text: The lab results are all normal, which helps rule out substance use or metabolic issues. Since you mentioned feeling depressed before these beliefs started, have you experienced any periods of unusually high energy, decreased need for sleep, or racing thoughts? speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient denies manic symptoms, and the lack of family history is noted, but the presentation of persecutory delusions and disorganized behavior for 6 weeks in a previously healthy 26-year-old male is highly suggestive of a primary psychotic disorder. I will request neuroimaging to rule out structural causes before finalizing the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI brain is normal, which effectively rules out structural lesions like tumors or abscesses as the cause of your psychosis. Given the duration of symptoms is six weeks—exceeding the one-month threshold for brief psychotic disorder but less than six months for schizophrenia—and the presence of prominent delusions and disorganized behavior, the clinical picture points toward schizophreniform disorder.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophreniform disorder
